snippet.title: New Twilight Princess VR updates! 6DOF, Third-Person, Right-Handed sword, Wolf Camera, and more!
snippet.description:
TPVR is coming along nicely, with many updates since the 1.0 release! Some of the big features are 6DOF positional tracking so you can move around in your space, a VR settings menu plus Dusklight menu support in VR, right-handed sword wielding, a fully fledged third-person mode, and an improved Wolf Camera, which now plays from Midna's perspective.

Huuuuge thank you to everybody who has played, discussed, and shared this mod. It genuinely means so much to me to create something for my favorite franchise and see so much excitement and support from so many different users!

Download on Github: https://github.com/JoeyAW/TPVR/releases

Join the Discord to report bugs, get help, and request features. https://discord.gg/CxQJ9PjnjA


Full changelog:

• Changed the mod name and logo to TPVR
• 6DOF tracking for gameplay, Wolf Mode, cutscenes and scene transitions
• New Wolf Mode camera. Instead of being stuck in 3rd person, you now play as a wolf from Midna's perspective on Link's back.
• Fixed a crash when pulling out the Gale Boomerang in the forest temple
• The Dusklight overlay now works in VR, accessible by holding down RS and the right trigger together for a couple seconds
• A new VR specific settings tab, accessible under Settings/VR.
• A toggleable third person mode. Fully compatible with a regular gamepad, third person mode allows you to experience the game without the need for VR controllers or 6DOF. While in this mode, aiming is tracked to the headset's direction, rather than the right controller.
• The option to show Link's body. Off by default, this shows Link's player model 
• An experimental first person camera option. Cutscenes are now third person by default, and this setting reverts that change.
• A right-handed sword toggle. This allows you to hold the sword in your right hand and the shield in your left, similar to the Wii version of the game, with motion controls swapped as well.
• Smooth rotation on the right stick for regular controllers.
• The reticle now gets bigger the further away it is from the camera across all items, helping maintain visibility when aiming for further targets such as the monkey or beehive with the owl.
• The camera now faces the right way when it changes shots in cutscenes. If the camera quickly changes direction, such as showing another angle, the headset view now snaps to that rotation. This is helpful for quick angle changes, but does not effect smooth camera movements.
• The camera faces Link when L/Z Targeting if third person mode is enabled.
• Transitions between areas are now in third person to prevent visual bugs, even when third person is disabled.
• Properly fixed the gamma/brightness issue
